# lock-closures roadmap

| O1 | How the chance that a lock closes moves with the upstream river-gauge level | A | 1 | measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | A 7-day closure-risk outlook for each lock from the river-level forecast | A | 2 | one model run a day, small once O1's model exists; basis: Stage 1's measured fit time |

Tracks: A — lock closures (research). One track, as confirmed 2026-11-06.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Closure chance against gauge level
      Objective: Estimate, from real closure records and real upstream gauge readings, how the chance of a lock closure moves with gauge level.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing; the repository holds an empty `lock_closures` package and one import smoke test
      Produces: a fitted closure-versus-gauge-level relation that later stages can reuse; `specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md`, recording the result and the measured cost
      Exit: the findings file reports how closure chance moves with upstream gauge level, estimated from real closure and gauge data, and records the measured cost of the real run: wall-clock time to acquire and fit, and the data volume used
      Leaves out: traceability: suggested, see the approval question; separate per-lock curves pooled across all 14 locks: Ranked list item O3
      ROUTING: brainstorming

---

The roadmap above is ready to write as `specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md`. I'll commit it on `main` once you approve. It commits one stage, the core stage for O1. It runs on real closure and gauge data and records its measured cost. O2, O3 and O4 wait in the Ranked list in your order. At a resume after Stage 1, the findings and cost come back to you for a re-rank.

**One question.** Do you approve this partition as written? It includes one suggested quality:

- **Traceability.** It goes in the Ranked list as an O5. The board will ask which gauge readings each closure estimate came from.
- Its outcome line would be: *"O5. For every closure estimate, a record of exactly which gauge readings it was computed from."*
- If you approve it, say where it ranks among O2, O3 and O4. If you don't want it, decline it.

You can also amend anything else in the same answer. One thing I should have raised earlier: O4, the history map for boat operators, doesn't depend on O1's model and serves a different audience. If you'd rather it not wait behind the research, it could be its own track. Otherwise I'll leave it ranked last as you said.

Once you answer, I'll record it, commit, and give you the "Next:" line for Stage 1 in a fresh session.
